subject.title: Add atomic claim/lease primitives for concurrent cron job dispatch and removal

question: Which public cron precondition should OpenClaw expose for concurrent dispatch/removal: narrow CAS/if-unclaimed remove, full lease-token dispatch, or documented current behavior with no new API?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable public contract affects Gateway schema, CLI flags, exit codes, docs, and external automation semantics.

options.title: Add narrow claim-aware remove
options.body: Add an additive --if-unclaimed or expected-version remove contract with a documented conflict exit and tests before considering full lease-token payloads.

options.title: Design full dispatch leases
options.body: Expose lease tokens on dispatch/show/remove so external callers can validate or revoke in-flight work at the cost of a larger public API.

options.title: Document no precondition API
options.body: Keep cron remove unconditional, document idempotent cleanup expectations, and close this direction as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Add narrow claim-aware remove
recommendation.body: Add an additive --if-unclaimed or expected-version remove contract with a documented conflict exit and tests before considering full lease-token payloads.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest inspected history on the cron scheduler and public cron surfaces affected by this API choice.
